title: The next game by the creators of Steins;Gate is an entirely vibe-coded FPS slopfest
summary: At least it's free, mostly.
body: Juggernaut is a forthcoming free-to-play boomer shooter clearly styled after Wolfenstein engine FPSes of yore. It's about shooting huge waves of zombies in flat, pixellated arenas. As far as modern retro shooters go it looks unremarkable, though it will be released alongside the Juggernaut Assets Maker, a paid tool for making your own levels and adding your own assets. "Make it more Japanese" the Steam page promises. "Make it sexier". It's the work of Mages Inc, a Japanese studio best known for the Steins;Gate series of visual novels; it has also worked on recent iterations of the Corpse Party series. Mages Inc generally specialises in visual novels, though it has released at least one Xbox 360 action game that was never released outside of Japan. But to what extent Mages Inc can actually be credited (or blamed) for their first foray into the first-person shooter genre is ripe for debate, because here's Juggernaut's AI Disclosure: AI Breakdown Source code: 100% Graphics: 60% Sound: 50% Effects: 100% In other words, this FPS is entirely vibe-coded, and its assets are overwhelmingly the work of generative AI. The Juggernaut Asset Maker , which will cost money, carries a similar disc…

title: Attendees will be able to check out a demo of The Witcher 3 DLC Songs of the Past behind closed doors at PAX Australia
summary: It's not that far away, come on.
body: I'm looking forward to an expansion for a game from 2015 more than I am for pretty much any new game coming up. The Songs of the Past add-on for The Witcher 3, which will be out next year, promises to let us explore a whole new region and get to know Dandelion better than ever. I'm more interested in a brand new chunk of world than intimate moments with the bard, but more Witcher 3 is more Witcher 3 even if the focus isn't on everyone's actual favorite character. (Johnny the Godling, of course.) Songs of the Past was shown off at Gamescom, where our Joshua Wolens had a peek and said it looked real good . The rest of us will have to wait for other opportunities, like the one that's been announced as part of the PAX Australia schedule reveal. On Saturday, October 11, attendees will be able to join members of CD Projekt and DLC developer Fool's Theory for a behind-closed-doors live demo of Songs of the Past, and a panel discussion to follow. title: How to mine the petrified Gammeltroll in Valheim
summary: The Deep North's big brute doesn't fall down when he dies. Here's what to do about it.
body: Have you met Valheim 1.0's mountainous menace, the Gammeltroll? If you've made your way to Valheim's final biome, the Deep North, you've probably seen and fought it already: the Gammeltroll is a 30-foot tall rock monster who pelts you with tree trunks from range and stomps you into paste if you get too close. Most interestingly, when you defeat the Gammeltroll, it doesn't fall down. Instead, it turns into a statue called a "Petrified Gammeltroll." You can chip away at its legs all you want, but even the toughest pickaxe in the game won't make a dent. And as you might have guessed, inside the Gammeltroll awaits a critical new resource you'll need to conquer the frozen biome. So, how do you mine it? title: Ikea made a Skyrim mod starring Matt Berry as a sentient shelf named Kallax Storageborn
summary: The mod includes a new quest, companion, and items—and as marketing stunts go, it looks pretty good.
body: The brands are at it again but this time I'm inclined to let it slide, because it's so nonsensical (which is a nice way of saying dumb ) that I can't help but be charmed. Ikea, the Swedish furniture-and-stuff giant, has released a mod for Skyrim called Kallax Storageborn: A new companion who is also a shelf, who is also voiced by Matt Berry. If you think that sounds weird, it gets weirder, because this mod doesn't just add a companion, it includes an entirely new questline built around the character. Becoming encumbered in the game, as will inevitably happen eventually, will give you the opportunity to visit an abandoned dwemer emporium, where you'll embark upon a quest to "unravel the origins of a mysterious master." During this quest, you'll assemble Kallax Storageborn, a companion "with unfathomable storage capacity," who can be summoned with a newly-added Thu'um—Skyrim's famous voice of power—even when he's not your active companion. Your ultimate goal: Tidy up the clutter plaguing the realm of Nords and Dragonborn. The mod also adds new loot including the Meatball Helmet, which sadly I don't have an image of, and the mighty Allenblade, which I do: (Image credit: Bethesda) The…

summary: The ASUS ROG Strix SCAR 18 feeds potent components with ample power into a brilliant display for a next-level gaming experience on the go.
body: If you're shopping around to get ready for the new school year and looking for a gaming laptop to cover a broad range of performance needs, you'll find plenty of hardware claiming it's for "gaming," but just what kind of gaming experience you'll get is still a huge question. title: 20 years later, veteran WoW director says players outsmarted him completely in Ahn'Qiraj: 'All that work, and there was still an instant tell'
summary: You better Skeram, kiddo.
body: I don't envy the position of being a game developer—especially not an encounter designer in something as complicated as an MMO. You might have an idea of how a mechanic's gonna go, but there's just absolutely no way it survives contact with 40 motivated, mid-2000s era hardcore WoW players. Former game director at Blizzard Wyatt Cheng, whose delightful TikTok channel has been giving free wisdom and anecdotes for some time now , says that exact agony happened to him around 20 years ago with the release of Ahn'Qiraj. Particularly with The Prophet Skeram boss, which splits into illusions at 75%, 50%, and 25% health. "There's one part I never got right," says Cheng. "I really wanted the only way to tell the difference between the real Skeram and the copies to be that the copies have half the health. So under even DPS rates, the illusions would drop in health faster." "I pictured raids spreading their DPS and calling it out on [Ventrilo]: Which two are going down quicker?" The idea being, if you didn't kill the illusions first, you'd knock the main Skeram over into his next health threshold and take on additional copies before you're ready: "Now there are five Skerams, and you wipe." Al…

title: 'Where is Nvidia? Call Nvidia, guys': Meltgate be damned, modders discover RTX 5090 can use 8-pin connectors after all
summary: The connectors seem to run fine above spec.
body: Ah yes, melty cables. We've been dealing with them ever since the RTX 4090 pushed the 16-pin 12VHPWR connector (now the 12V-2x6 connector) to its limits. Since then, we've heard of numerous cases of melting GPU connectors—check out Uniko's Hardware on X for many examples—and plenty of attempts at dealing with them. Now, some modders have said 'screw it' to the new 12V-2x6 design, instead modding an RTX 5090 to run on standard 8-pin connectors (via Wccftech ). The modders at TecLab fitted three 8-pin connectors to the back of the PCB using "copper plates, cut by hand", and hooked these up to the front via 24 cables (3x sets of 8). Once everything was also unlocked to operate at higher power levels, the graphics card was put to the test. And while this was just one batch of tests with one card (and don't try this at home, folks) the results were fantastic. Even before pushing it as far as it eventually goes, the modders were thrilled with the results (machine translated): "It's getting warmer. It's still colder than a 12VHPWR connector. It's colder than the original connector, guys. Where is Nvidia? Call Nvidia, guys. Put the raw footage out there for people to see, otherwise they'l…

title: Turns out, a lot of Sega's biggest fans don't play its videogames: 'In some cases, their engagement is even higher than that of fans who actually play'
summary: Nah-kuza.
body: There once was a time in which, if you were a fan of a videogame, you might get asked which of said games in the series you had played. Now, I'm not saying we need to bring this era back—it was an obnoxious period full of gatekeepers—but Sega president and COO Shuji Utsumi's recent words on the subject are a surprising sign of the times. Speaking to Nikkei Gaming (thanks, IGN ), Utsumi explains that (via machine translation): "For example, the 'Yakuza' series has been doing exceptionally well in merchandising, with 60-70% of its buyers being women. They've become fans of the 'Yakuza' world, story, and characters after watching our YouTube channel and popular YouTubers' streams. And among them are many people who have never actually played the game." I'm assuming that Utsumi has stats to back that up, rather than just assuming that women don't play videogames (they do, I work with several of them), but it's indeed true that videogames have been enjoying a wider secondary audience thanks to let's players and streamers. "Even people who have never played games are considered fans and 'gamers' by us," he adds, "transmedia's strength lies in increasing the entry points and contact poin…

title: Marvel Rivals breaks its 17 month streak of adding 2 heroes per season, but its creative director reassures fans it's not 'the new normal'
summary: Season 10 brings one hero, two new game modes, and masses of balance changes.
body: Marvel Rivals ' massive hero roster and regular character additions are some of its defining features. So it comes as a huge surprise that NetEase has decided to forgo tradition for the sake of focusing on improving its foundations. For the first time in eight seasons—that's 17 months—Marvel Rivals will just be getting one hero, Gorr the God Butcher, in a season. "We're locking our crosshairs on just Gorr the God Butcher," creative designer Guangyun Chen says in a dev diary . "In the first half of the season we'll be rolling out one new hero and one new map. In the second half our focus will shift to phase 3 and phase 4 of the Path to Doomsday events. These will feature two brand-new game modes, with specific details dropping closer to the start of season 10.5." Marvel Rivals doesn't have a creative block when it comes to inventign new heroes—it's got a huge backlog of characters at its disposal. But two new heroes per season does put considerable strain on the game's balance. Traditionally, new heroes are completely busted when they're first added to Marvel Rivals. This is due to NetEase's "fun first" approach , but also because of the serious backlog of fixes that preoccupies th…

title: Valheim Deep North: How to get the Intricate Key
summary: Locked castle doors in Valheim 1.0 can only be opened by a hard-to-get item.
body: As a mighty Viking warrior you've fought your way to the Deep North in Valheim 1.0—but now you're facing an enormous door that requires an Intricate Key to unlock. But what is an Intricate Key in Valheim, and how can you get one? Truth is, you'll eventually need more than one Intricate Key to triumph in the Deep North, so here's a quick guide that'll walk you through the steps to find them. How to craft an Intricate Key in Valheim 1.0 (Image credit: Coffee Stain Publishing) As you explore the Deep North, keep an eye out for small, snow-covered villages. Look for the largest building in the village, a multi-story dwelling , seen in the image above, then head inside. Explore the interior until you find a large hole in the floor . Jump in to enter the hidden tunnels . Be prepared to fight: the hidden tunnels are filled with enemies. Look for Frostcores , they look like glowing blue ice and are typically overhead. Collect any moulds you find in the tunnels, especially moulds for the Intricate Key. Important notes: Moulds look like flat black rectangles with shapes etched into them. title: Should you start a new character and world for Valheim 1.0?
summary: Advice from the developers and PC Gamer on how to play the completed version of Valheim.
body: Valheim 1.0 is here, so that sound you hear in the distance is scores of eager Vikings stringing their bows, sharpening their axes, and piling onto their longboats to explore the open world survival game's final biome: the Deep North. But before you set sail for some chilly thrills in the frosty new biome, you might be wondering if you should create a new character and generate a new world for Valheim 1.0, or just keep playing with your current Viking and world. Veteran Valheimers will know that updates can conflict with existing worlds: any areas you've already explored, for example, won't be overwritten with new terrain and features, which can sometimes cause problems. So, should you start fresh or continue from where you left off? Let's begin with what the devs advise: "As usual, your world will receive new content even if it was created before the update, although biome generation will only work properly on areas that have not yet been explored," says developer Iron Gate in its Valheim 1.0 FAQ . "However, we always recommend that you start the game over from scratch to get the best possible experience." In other words, if you've already explored the areas to the far north of y…

title: 'No-one puts Double Fine out of business except me', says Tim Schafer on taking Double Fine independent: 'Asha's not going to shoot my dog'
summary: "The games industry is full of terrible things, and I can't change most of them."
body: Double Fine has ducked out of the way of Microsoft's falling axe, going independent after the new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced layoffs totalling 3,200 people earlier this year. The studio itself has had a bit of a troubled discography after the win of Psychonauts 2, with neither 2025's Keeper or 2026's Kiln doing much to move the needle. Tim Schafer pretty much pins his studio's voluntary exile from Microsoft on Sharma in a conversation with Bloomberg , saying that the storm clouds first started gathering when she visited the studio in "listening mode"—but it was clear that, when she started talking about shifting Xbox's vision, it was bad news. "We had a mutually beneficial mission," says Schafer, "Which is just to put great games on Game Pass, and then their mission changed. I can't imagine any amount of profitability—unless we had a breakout, Minecraft hit that year—would've saved us." You're reading this article because Double Fine didn't do that, though Schafer doesn't seem to have any major hard feelings about it: "The games industry is full of terrible things, and I can't change most of them. title: Wi-Fi 8 is upon us, so here are two routers we saw at Computex that should be hitting the shops soon
summary: Unsurprisingly, Asus ROG is launching its Wi-Fi 8 routers with an extreme gaming monster.
body: Last week at IFA 2026 TP-Link announced two new Wi-Fi 8 routers —the Archer 9 Ultra and the Deco 8 Ultra—though the actual price and release date aren’t yet known, other than availability being later this year. While TP-Link claimed these are the first Wi-Fi 8 routers to be revealed, this isn't quite the case: Asus showed off its Wi-Fi 8 ROG Rapture GT-BN98 at Computex in June, and we were there having a proper gawk. This is a premium gaming router that’s loaded up with features and game optimisations, and with classic completely-OTT ROG looks. Asus also showed its more mainstream ZenWiFi BN12 at Computex for normal people. Pricing and availability have not yet been announced—though review samples of the ROG Rapture GT-BN98 are expected to be available very soon, so it’s not far off. Wi-Fi 8 isn’t so much about boosting speed over Wi-Fi 7: stability under heavy load is the main objective of the new standard, as we continue to saturate the Wi-Fi airwaves with ever more demanding uses. Compared to Wi-Fi 7, the new Wi-Fi 8 standard is far from being a premium speed boost for the sake of it like past Wi-Fi iterations, and is more of a user experience enhancement that addresses some of…

title: Corporations want to kill physical media because it suits them, but Big Box PC game packaging just got a second chance
summary: It's now much easier to take the DIY approach.
body: If you were alive and sentient in the nineties you probably harbour some fondness for the "big box" PC games of yore. Back then, rather than buy an ephemeral digital license for a game, you'd head to a store to buy a huge box bedecked in lavish art, inside which you'd find a handful of 3.5-inch floppy discs or a CD-ROM, usually a substantial glossy manual, and if you were lucky, maybe even some extras like stickers or drink coasters. There's been renewed interest in the ye olde big box PC game, especially in the wake of Sony's announcement it will discontinue physical PlayStation games. Some proactive folk have gone viral for manufacturing their own physical Steam games . Now GOG has offered its own alternative: printable big boxes based on scans of real commercial packages from the golden era of game packaging. In collaboration with Big Box Collection—which is a fan-operated trove of big box 3D scans—GOG is now offering those 3D scans with five entries in its GOG Preservation Program. These include the newly added Star Trek: 25th Anniversary and Armikrog, while games already in the Preservation Program including Descent, Hitman: Codename 47, and Myst will also receive the treatme…

title: Less than a week after launch, The Blood of Dawnwalker developer is already getting to work on the sequel
summary: Rebel Wolves is hiring.
body: With more than one million copies sold just a few days after its release, a "very positive" rating on Steam, and an enviable 83% review score from PC Gamer, vampiric horror RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker is a hit. And less than one week after its debut, developer Rebel Wolves is already planning what comes next. Unsurprisingly, "what comes next" is more Dawnwalker: Jakub Szamałek, narrative director at developer Rebel Wolves, wrote on LinkedIn (via Dexerto ) that "we're not resting on our laurels," but are already thinking about where to take the game from here. "I'm looking for a lead writer to help me and the narrative team craft the next chapter in the Dawnwalker saga," Szamałek wrote. "We're looking for someone who, to put it bluntly, writes EXCEPTIONALLY well, has a track record of excellence and experience in team management." The job listing provides more detail about what's involved and it's heavy stuff, with responsibilities ranging from writing in-game documents and dialog to collaborating with the narrative director—that's Szamałek—and other team leads, and managing the entire writers team. You'll also need "a minimum of six years of experience as a writer/narrative design…

title: Thousand Hells is a 'tactical narrative' feast of infernal storytelling, but its defeats can feel brutal
summary: From the developer of King of Dragon Pass, a gorgeously imagined meat grinder for hapless adventuring parties.
body: In Thousand Hells: The Underworld heists, I've sort of taken on the role of the dad in that one tweet about feeding cats to coyotes. But rather than serving up pets to jackals, I'm dutifully feeding bands of doomed adventurers into the psychological, corporeal, and spiritual wood chipper of the "tactical narrative" game's bespoke hellscapes. Those hellscapes—from the primordial twilight taigas of the Midnight North, to the melting fever-dream dominion of the Hell of Nightmares—form a mesmerizing kaleidoscope of abyssal imagination. Made by the developer behind the phenomenal King of Dragon Pass and Six Ages games , its pedigree is obvious as each game guides my hand-picked party of hell raiders through encounters rich with the implied culture, tradition, and history of their respective afterlives. I just wish I weren't spending quite as much time feeling like my efforts are futile. (Image credit: Kitfox Games) A game of Thousand Hells, designed for quicker, more repeatable sessions than developer A Sharp's prior work, begins in the Eternal City, a metropolis where the thousand worlds conjoin, and from which daring (or foolish) heroes can embark for their thousand associated underw…

title: Over 1,000 cut voice lines from Resident Evil 4 and Requiem reveal more about Leon Kennedy, the zombies he fights, and a lowkey bromance
summary: We also got some hints to how later games are linked to Resident Evil 4.
body: Resident Evil is one of those series which rewards nosey players. There's always notes, recordings, and pictures hidden in the cracks and crevices, all of which give players more info. Whether that be the structural integrity, of Mr. X's trench coat or the fact that Grace Ashcroft has absolutely zero social life. But it's not just all about notes—there's also a great deal of information given in Resident Evil games via their seemingly throwaway voice lines. So, with that in mind, one leaker has just found the motherlode. (Image credit: Capcom) Notable community modder Keff0 has posted two videos to YouTube over the last week. One goes through over 600 cut voice lines from the Resident Evil 4 remake , and the other explores nearly 400 cut voice lines from Resident Evil Requiem . The Resident Evil 4 remake deep dive into the scrapped voice lines is certainly interesting, as we hear more from Leon, Ashley, Luis, and the Merchant. Hearing more from Leon is always a win, but the prize for 'most notable cut voice' line has to go to the Merchant, as he sneaks in a reference to Resident Evil Village . "Ah, I see you're no stranger to villages," the Merchant says in a cut line from the RE4…

title: Our absolute favourite gaming keyboard, the Wooting 80HE, is getting a BIG KNOB, improved switches, and more
summary: This could become the new best gaming keyboard.
body: The Wooting 80HE has been out for a while, but we reckon it's still the best gaming keyboard on the market. It looks great, isn't too diminutively sized, has fantastic and very customisable software, and, of course, Hall effect switches for adjustable actuation and rapid trigger. All for a pretty reasonable price, mind you. And now it's getting an upgrade Wooting has just announced the Wooting 80HE+ , available for pre-order on September 17. That's a week on Thursday. There are a number of changes coming to the new 'Plus' version, including of course the addition of a BIG KNOB, but also some less visible but arguably more important changes. Specifically, I'm talking about the inclusion of the same Lekker Tikken switches that you'll find in the Wooting 60HE V2 . Our Jacob Ridley has really taken to this keyboard and its switches, as it's much more stable and generally pleasant-sounding and -feeling than the Lekker60 V2 switches in the original 80HE. Combine this with the new FR4 plate inside the 80HE+ and you can almost certainly expect a wonderful typing experience. The best just became better 🌟The Wooting 80HE+ is joining the Wooting roster soon!Wanna be up to date and the first…

title: I got my hands on Razer's new $50 mechanical mini keeb and it makes a damn good first impression
summary: It's got an entry-level MSRP, but still feels like an enthusiast-level device.
body: Razer had a bountiful display of products to show at Gamescom 2026, many of which come with substantial price tags. However, my eyes lit up when I saw the new Razer Reclusa X Mini 65% keyboard , especially as it's got a $50/£60 MSRP. I picked it up and twisted it around in my hands, expecting it to bend like a piece of cardboard thanks to some budget materials. Nope, it seems like a very solidly-built device—which is pretty impressive given the affordable price tag. The doubleshot ABS keycaps, in combination with Razer's Gen-3 orange tactile switches , feel downright high-end. It makes a good noise, too, producing the sort of weighty thock I normally associate with much more expensive keebs. I've used enough $50 boards to know that you usually don't get a whole lot for your cash, but this one feels like a proper enthusiast offering—even if it does come in a shrunken 65% form factor. The switches are hot-swappable, with both 3-pin and 5-pin models supported. The orange ones it comes with are designed to deliver a "crisp, satisfying tactile bump without the click," according to the press release, and I can confirm this to be true. I hate overly-clicky tactile switches, but these are…

title: Why does this sort of thing never happen to me? Redditor says they found $10,000 worth of RAM just sitting in their garage
summary: This memory stash doesn't grant an automatic upgrade for their gaming rig, though.
body: Found 10k worth of ram sitting in my garage from r/LinusTechTips As the spawn of two IT professionals, my childhood home is still steeped in a whole lot of old hardware. It's amazing what my folks have lying around—but I very much doubt they've got a horde of RAM they've just neglected to tell me about. One Redditor recently revealed they have roughly $10,000 AUD (about $7,200 USD) worth of RAM squirrelled away in their garage. The stash appears to contain multiple 64GB DDR4 sticks. The poster said in a follow-up comment that this small fortune came from "an old work server that they let me keep." Some hardware professionals get all the luck. PC gamers should be no strangers to how much memory servers can gobble up, with at least some of the blame for our present memory crisis moment resting on the shoulders of AI data centres. Worse still, not all server memory will be compatible with your rig; modern desktop PCs tend to use UDIMMs, whereas servers use RDIMMs— Corsair breaks down the differences here . Basically, if the AI bubble bursts tomorrow, leaving lots of server memory floating around in its wake, that wouldn't automatically be great news for your gaming rig. Today, if you…

title: Valheim 1.0 review
summary: Your long journey is at an end, Viking.
body: Need to know What is it? A Viking-themed survival game set in a procedurally generated open world. Release date : September 09, 2026 (1.0) Expect to pay : $30/£23.49 Developer : Iron Gate AB Publisher : Coffee Stain Publishing Reviewed on : Intel i7 9700K, RTX 4070 Ti, 16GB RAM Steam Deck : Verified Link : Official site After a day-long battle with one of Valheim's big bosses, I return to my modest cabin in the woods to recover. I'm exhausted, my weapons and armor are mostly broken, and I've burned through my meager supply of food and arrows. I don't even have a spare torch left to light my way home. Even though I was victorious, the cold and rainy night doesn't put me in the mood for a celebration. Then I spot a shadowy figure in the gloom, leaning on a walking stick, one blue eye gleaming from beneath its hood. Odin . It's frickin' Odin himself, y'know, Thor's dad? title: SteelSeries throws everything but the kitchen sink in the feature list of its Aeon Pro controller
summary: It can seamlessly switch between Xbox and PC, but is very expensive.
body: Last month I got to take a look at what SteelSeries calls the "world’s first dual-dock controller built for PC and Xbox": the Aeon Pro. Its dual-docking claim to fame is that it allows you to switch between PC and Xbox gameplay seamlessly, without re-pairing. That's thanks to dual USB inputs on the base station, one connected to PC and the other to Xbox. The thing is, that feature itself sounds pretty niche to my diminutive ears, given there probably aren't tons of PC gamers also using Xbox (though I am open to being corrected on that). Instead, I'm much more interested in what else the controller has to offer, and for what cost. On this front, we're looking at a *gulp* $260/£230/€260 price tag, which places it firmly in top-end territory at least as far as its pricing is concerned. Having had my hands on it—albeit only briefly—I can say it does feel like a premium controller, with pretty solid build quality, great grips, and comfy button presses. I'm not a fan of the ABXY buttons, however, as they feel slightly mushy for my tastes, but only in the same way that some other premium controllers are and that others seem to not mind.
